terms.gloss: hold; hold the attention of, fascinate
evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.48: pompā, lūdīs atque ejus modī spectāculīs teneantur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Ac. 2.20: ut oculī pictūrā teneantur, aurēs cantibus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In this sense mostly passive: to be held, enchained by a sight or a sound (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Off. 3.15: quod capiat ignārōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To win someone over, often with the ablative of what does it (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: bewitch, cast the evil eye on
terms.comment: A false friend: classically to bewitch by an evil eye or tongue, not to interest (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: ut pompā, lūdīs atque ejus modī spectāculīs teneantur ob eamque rem vel famem et sitim perferant
phrases.english: (children) are so held by a parade, games and such shows that for their sake they will bear even hunger and thirst

phrases.latin: nesciō quis tenerōs oculus mihi fascinat agnōs
phrases.english: some eye or other is bewitching my tender lambs

sources: Lewis & Short: teneo · Lewis & Short: capio · Lewis & Short: fascino
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.
